summary.headline: Neogen Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR 250 crore, EBITDA up 53% to INR 48 crore, with margin at 19.3%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 250 crore grew 34% YoY, led by organo-lithium, inorganic chemicals and battery chemicals, with record quarterly revenue in organo-lithium and battery chemicals. EBITDA rose 53% to INR 48.2 crore and margin expanded 260 bps to 19.3% despite Dahej rebuild, toll manufacturing and Neogen Ionics start-up costs. PAT rose 67% to INR 17.1 crore. Management raised standalone FY27 revenue guidance to INR 950-1,050 crore from INR 875-950 crore and approved a INR 600 crore QIP mainly for debt reduction.

segments.name: Organo-lithium / organic chemicals
segments.commentary: Organic chemicals revenue INR 194 crore (+18% YoY); organo-lithium capacity (raised 2.5x to 300 tpa) hit full utilisation in Q1. Of the ~INR 67 crore YoY revenue increase in the legacy business, management said ~INR 15 crore was price-driven and the rest volume.

segments.name: Inorganic chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 57 crore, up 158% YoY, benefiting from by-product lithium recycling linked to organo-lithium growth.

segments.name: Battery chemicals (Neogen Ionics)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 19 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 5 crore in Q1 FY26, over 50% of FY26 full-year revenue; largely salts. FY27 battery revenue guidance kept at ~INR 300 crore (INR 200 crore salt, INR 100 crore electrolyte).

guidance_outlook: Standalone FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR 950-1,050 crore from INR 875-950 crore; base business expected to cross INR 1,000 crore.
Base business EBITDA margin guided at 18% +/-1-1.5% for FY27; FY28 guided at 19% +/-1-1.5%.

Battery chemicals FY27 revenue guided at ~INR 300 crore, mostly in H2 as US customers shift to non-FEOC supply from January 2027; upside if India ACC PLI cell output ramps faster or Pakhajan contributes in Q4.
Battery electrolyte commissioning targeted H1 FY27; lithium electrolyte salts H2 FY27. Dahej replacement plant commercial production expected in Q2 FY27.
Battery capacity full utilisation targeted FY29 at INR 2,400-2,900 crore revenue; ~20% ROCE targeted on ~INR 1,800 crore capex.
Base business FY28 revenue expected at INR 1,100-1,200 crore (10-15% growth); battery FY28 revenue expected above INR 1,000 crore, to be updated at year-end.
Peak net debt expected INR 1,000-1,500 crore post QIP; QIP-driven interest saving estimated INR 40-50 crore annually if fully repaid, at 8-8.5% rates.
Insurance: cumulative recoveries INR 164 crore; net claim receivable INR 186 crore.
capex_capacity: Battery capex ~INR 1,800 crore; management said ~INR 1,300 crore spent (per analyst, CFO to confirm), with full completion targeted by end FY27; balance funded by debt, Morita equity (USD 20 million, Q2-Q3 FY27) and INR 30-50 crore Neogen equity.
Pakhajan site: 30 GWh-equivalent salt and electrolyte start, with room to scale to ~100 GWh; electrolyte plant mechanical assembly complete and trials initiated.
Spare capacity: ~2,000 tpa salt at Pakhajan and ~500 tpa additives at Dahej (~2.5 ktpa) can be added in 18-24 months from decision.
Organo-lithium incremental capex of INR 10-15 crore under consideration, board proposal around end Q2 FY27.
CSM expansion: dedicated investment likely FY29-FY30, contingent on Dahej restart and customer testing in FY27.
demand_pricing: Four international customers have provisionally approved lithium electrolyte salts; site audits completed at all four electrolyte makers. Commercial supply starts after final plant trial approvals.
Management has worked with 5 of 6 large Indian gigafactories; four of six expected to start this year and two next year, with combined capacity over 60 GWh.

Salt pricing is formula-based on lithium carbonate at a stable ~USD 20/kg +/- USD 5 band; lithium is passed through to customers. Near-term Q2-Q3 volumes may carry special pricing slightly below formula as China spot is below formula price.
Management says battery sales to US customers will be on contracted, non-FEOC terms from Q4 FY27; US tax credit (45X) requirements drive the shift.

Organo-lithium demand is multi-industry, with pharma the largest end-use, followed by semiconductor (new approval) and agro. Customer base has expanded to many customers from one major product and three or four customers at takeover.
CSM demand remains engaged but no progress since the Dahej fire; large-molecule target INR 50-100 crore per molecule.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5 crore in Q1 FY26

qa_highlights.question: How big can battery chemicals be in five years, and is China's technology restriction a risk to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pegged current capex capacity at INR 2,400-2,900 crore revenue at full utilisation by FY29, linked to ~30 GWh electrolyte and ~40 GWh salt; longer-term sizing not guided. Said no dependency on China for technology (Japanese partner Morita tech), and sodium-ion seen as niche with the same plant usable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery revenue guidance for FY27 and how is it split?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 300 crore kept: ~INR 200 crore salt and ~INR 100 crore electrolyte, mostly in H2 as US customers shift to non-FEOC supply from January 2027; Pakhajan not included in guidance and is the buffer for electrolyte shortfall.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing underpins the salt revenue and how does spot price affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Salt priced off a lithium-carbonate formula with stable band of USD 20/kg +/- 5, lithium passed through. Q2-Q3 volumes may carry special pricing slightly below formula because China spot is below formula; the gap has narrowed versus 2024-25.

qa_highlights.question: Is the legacy guidance raise driven by price or volume, and what drove organo-lithium?
qa_highlights.answer: Organo-lithium capacity raised 2.5x to 300 tpa and hit full utilisation in Q1. Of the ~INR 15 crore price-driven share of legacy growth, the rest was volume; further small capacity add (INR 10-15 crore capex) to be proposed around end Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the uses of the INR 600 crore QIP and the finance cost benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly debt reduction as a temporary measure, with optionality for battery PLI, international demand, organo-lithium capacity and R&D. If fully repaid, annual interest saving of ~INR 40-50 crore at 8-8.5%; peak net debt ~INR 1,000-1,500 crore post QIP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base business guidance and EBITDA margin outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Base business FY27 revenue INR 950-1,050 crore, expected to cross INR 1,000 crore; FY28 base revenue INR 1,100-1,200 crore (10-15% growth). Base EBITDA margin 18% +/-1-1.5% for FY27 and 19% +/-1-1.5% for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and cash-flow outlook, and how will the battery capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Battery business working capital cycle targeted at ~90 days versus ~140 days stabilised for base by FY28; management said FY29 should be a strong year for cash-flow conversion. Capex ~INR 1,800 crore to finish by end FY27, funded by debt, Morita USD 20 million equity and INR 30-50 crore Neogen equity; CFO to confirm whether INR 1,300 crore is already spent.

qa_highlights.question: Can the electrolyte and salt capacity expansions and US/international demand be scaled, and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Four international electrolyte makers approved Neogen's site and five of six large Indian gigafactories are engaged (combined over 60 GWh); spare capacity of ~2,000 tpa salt at Pakhajan and ~500 tpa additives at Dahej can be added in 18-24 months from decision, with a decision expected around end FY27 or early FY28.

risks_watch: Battery revenue back-end loaded: INR 300 crore FY27 guidance depends on US non-FEOC shift from January 2027 and on electrolyte plants (INR 100 crore) ramping on time; Pakhajan is the only buffer and is not in guidance.
Pricing risk: Q2-Q3 salt volumes may be sold at special pricing slightly below formula while China spot is below the formula price; lithium carbonate band assumed at USD 20/kg +/- 5.

Working capital and leverage: consolidated debt-equity cited at 1.4 vs standalone 0.68; peak net debt INR 1,000-1,500 crore post QIP; finance cost up 64% YoY; insurance net receivable INR 186 crore still to be settled.
Dahej replacement plant commercial production targeted in Q2 FY27; CSM business has shown no progress since the fire and dedicated CSM investment deferred to FY29-FY30.
Government battery PLI scheme not yet finalised; management declined to quantify benefit or pass-through to customers.
Organic/inorganic mix: inorganic revenue up 158% YoY partly from by-product lithium recycling; one-off benefit from older inventory in Q1 not quantified by management.

Watch next quarter: organo-lithium incremental capex board proposal (end Q2 FY27), Morita equity infusion timing, QIP completion, Neogen Ionics electrolyte commissioning (H1 FY27) and first US non-FEOC shipments.
key_quotes: Reconstruction of our replacement facility at Dahej is almost complete. Trial runs are actively underway with commercial production set to commence within the current Q2 FY27 quarter.
FY27 represents a strategic turning point for Neogen Chemicals as our capital investment transitions into revenue-generating assets.
So, even if they hit 50% utilization, we would reach our full utilization target.
I cannot promise consistently positive cash flows because Neogen will always be growing.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, capacity and the FY27 guidance raise, but cautious and hedged on timing, pricing and cash flow, repeatedly deferring specific numbers (battery FY28, PLI benefit, CSM capex, FCF) to year-end.
